```text
1	---
2	name: demo-evidence
3	description: Capture acceptance evidence — screenshots, terminal/screen recordings, HTTP logs — for a just-built feature into a gitignored .evidence/ bundle keyed to git branch/commit + coding-agent session, for async human validation (Cursor "Demos over diffs" style). Use when the user says "record a demo", "leave evidence", "capture a screenshot/video", "prove it works", wants async sign-off / 驗收, or asks to show a feature works without reading the diff or booting the app by hand. Playwright/asciinema/curl/ffmpeg.
4	---
5	
6	# demo evidence
7	
8	Reviewing an agent's work usually means reading the diff or booting the app
9	by hand. This skill has the agent **leave behind acceptance evidence** —
10	screenshots, screen/terminal recordings, request logs — filed into a
11	`.gitignore`-protected `.evidence/` tree, each bundle keyed to the git
12	branch/commit and the coding-agent session that produced it. A reviewer (or a
13	later agent) opens the bundle's `MANIFEST.md`, watches the demo, and signs off
14	— no re-driving the app.
15	
16	The lifecycle is three scripts: **`new-bundle.sh`** (open a bundle) →
17	**`capture.sh`** (add artifacts, once per surface) → **`finalize.sh`** (stamp a
18	verdict and render the review page). Complements the global `run` / `verify`
19	skills: use *those* to drive the app; use *this* to record what they showed.
20	
21	## When to use
22	
23	- User says "record a demo of this", "leave evidence", "capture a
24	  screenshot/video of the feature", "prove it works", "demos over diffs".
25	- User wants **async 驗收 / sign-off** — they'll review later, not watch you now.
26	- You just finished a feature and want the acceptance artifacts to live
27	  next to the branch/commit that produced them.
28	- A reviewer asked "show me it works" without reading the diff.
29	
30	## When NOT to use
31	
32	- The change has **no runtime surface** (docs, comments, pure refactor with
33	  tests) → nothing to demo; point at the tests.
34	- You just need to *drive* the app to check it yourself → global `run` /
35	  `verify`. Only reach here when you want a **filed, reviewable artifact**.
36	- Posting media **into a PR** → not in v1. `.evidence/` is gitignored, so its
37	  images/videos have no public URL to embed (see Gotchas). Tracked as a `P?`
38	  backlog item.
39	
40	## Workflow
41	
42	### 1. Open a bundle
43	
44	```bash
45	bash skills/local/demo-evidence/scripts/new-bundle.sh \
46	  --title "login flow" --feature "Verify login redirects to /dashboard"
47	# stdout: {"bundle_dir":".evidence/claude-5f932f43/2026-…-6526681-login-flow", ...}
48	```
49	
50	Detects the agent session + git branch/short-SHA/dirty, creates
51	`.evidence/<agent>-<session>/<UTC-ts>-<shortSHA>[-<title>]/`, writes
52	`manifest.json` + a `MANIFEST.md` scaffold, ensures `.evidence/` is gitignored,
53	and records the path in `.evidence/.current`. Later steps default to
54	`.current`, so you rarely pass `--bundle`.
55	
56	### 2. Capture one artifact per surface
57	
58	Pick the mode(s) that fit the app. Each appends to the bundle manifest.
59	
60	```bash
61	CAP="bash skills/local/demo-evidence/scripts/capture.sh"
62	
63	# Web UI — full-page screenshot + video + Playwright trace
64	$CAP web  --url http://localhost:3000/login --name login --steps ./demo-steps.mjs
65	
66	# CLI / TUI — asciinema recording (falls back to a plain tee'd log)
67	$CAP term --cmd "mytool --do-the-thing" --name run
68	
69	# HTTP / API — status + headers + body + timing
70	$CAP http --url http://localhost:8000/health --name health
71	
72	# Desktop / non-browser GUI — timed screen recording
73	$CAP screen --seconds 10 --name walkthrough
74	```
75	
76	Capture what actually demonstrates the feature — don't capture blindly. A
77	before/after screenshot pair or a 10-second flow beats a folder of noise.
78	
79	### 3. Finalize for review
80	
81	```bash
82	bash skills/local/demo-evidence/scripts/finalize.sh \
83	  --verdict PASS \
84	  --step "open /login" --step "submit valid creds" --step "expect /dashboard" \
85	  --scrub
86	```
87	
88	Stamps the verdict, appends reproduction steps, refreshes artifact sizes, runs
89	an optional secret scan, and renders the human-facing `MANIFEST.md` (verdict
90	badge, context, repro steps, artifact table, review checklist). Point the
91	reviewer at `<bundle>/MANIFEST.md`.
92	
93	## Available scripts
94	
95	- **`scripts/new-bundle.sh`** — Create a bundle keyed to session + git; emit its path as JSON. Guarantees `.evidence/` is gitignored.
96	  - Flags: `--title`, `--feature`, `--agent`, `--root`, `--dry-run`, `--help`.
97	  - Exit: `0` ok, `1` bad args, `2` not a git repo, `3` jq missing.
98	- **`scripts/capture.sh <web|term|http|screen>`** — Capture one artifact into a bundle (default `.current`) and record it in `manifest.json`.
99	  - Common: `--bundle`, `--root`, `--name`, `--note`, `--dry-run`.
100	  - `web`: `--url`, `--steps`, `--timeout`. `term`: `--cmd`, `--log`. `http`: `--url`, `--method`, `--data`, `--header` (repeatable). `screen`: `--seconds`, `--device`, `--display`.
101	  - Exit: `0` ok, `1` bad args, `2` no bundle, `3` jq missing, `4` capture tool missing, `5` capture failed.
102	- **`scripts/finalize.sh`** — Set verdict, append steps, refresh sizes, optional secret scan, render `MANIFEST.md`.
103	  - Flags: `--bundle`, `--root`, `--verdict PASS|NEEDS_WORK|pending`, `--step` (repeatable), `--scrub`, `--dry-run`, `--help`.
104	  - Exit: `0` ok, `1` bad args, `2` no bundle, `3` jq missing.
105	- **`scripts/detect-session.sh`** — Best-effort `{agent, session_id, source, specstory_path}` JSON. Standalone or called by `new-bundle.sh`.
106	  - Flags: `--agent`, `--json`/`--tsv`, `--quiet`, `--help`. Exit: `0` always, `1` bad args.
107	
108	## Bundled assets
109	
110	- `assets/capture-web.mjs` — Minimal Playwright runner (screenshot + video +
111	  trace) invoked by `capture.sh web`. Loads `playwright` from the project's
112	  `node_modules` via `createRequire(cwd)`.
113	
114	## Gotchas
115	
116	- **`.evidence/` media has NO public URL — it cannot embed in a GitHub PR.**
117	  The whole point is a gitignored local surface, so images/videos aren't
118	  web-reachable. Posting to a PR (gist-raw-URL image embed, video links) is a
119	  deliberate `P?` backlog item, out of scope for v1. For now, share the bundle
120	  locally or push it out-of-band.
121	- **Screenshots and logs can leak secrets, and screenshots can't be
122	  auto-scrubbed.** `finalize.sh --scrub` only *reports* on text artifacts
123	  (`*.log`, `*.txt`) via gitleaks — a human must eyeball images/video before
124	  sharing them anywhere. Because `.evidence/` is gitignored, nothing reaches
125	  git history, but external sharing is on you.
126	- **`capture.sh web` needs Node + Playwright installed in the project.** If
127	  `playwright` doesn't resolve from the CWD it exits `4` with an install hint
128	  (`npm i -D playwright && npx playwright install chromium`) — or use the
129	  `microsoft/playwright-cli` skill as the browser engine instead.
130	- **`capture.sh screen` on macOS needs Screen Recording permission** and the
131	  right avfoundation device index (default `1`, varies per machine). List
132	  devices with `ffmpeg -f avfoundation -list_devices true -i ""` and pass
133	  `--device`. On Linux it uses `x11grab` on `$DISPLAY`.
134	- **Agent detection is best-effort.** Env markers (`$CLAUDECODE`, `$CURSOR_*`,
135	  `$CODEX_*`) then artifact presence; falls back to `unknown`. Pass
136	  `--agent cursor|codex|…` to `new-bundle.sh` when the session isn't yours.
137	- **`term` falls back to a plain log without asciinema.** The log still
138	  captures stdout+stderr and the command's exit code, but not timing/replay.
139	  Install `asciinema` for a replayable `.cast`.
140	- **Bundles default to `.evidence/.current`.** Running a second `new-bundle.sh`
141	  repoints `.current`; pass `--bundle DIR` to capture into an older bundle.
142
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	---
2	name: demo-evidence
3	description: Capture acceptance evidence — screenshots, terminal/screen recordings, HTTP logs — for a just-built feature into a gitignored .evidence/ bundle keyed to git branch/commit + coding-agent session, for async human validation (Cursor "Demos over diffs" style). Use when the user says "record a demo", "leave evidence", "capture a screenshot/video", "prove it works", wants async sign-off / 驗收, or asks to show a feature works without reading the diff or booting the app by hand. Playwright/asciinema/curl/ffmpeg.
4	---
5	
6	# demo evidence
7	
8	Reviewing an agent's work usually means reading the diff or booting the app
9	by hand. This skill has the agent **leave behind acceptance evidence** —
10	screenshots, screen/terminal recordings, request logs — filed into a
11	`.gitignore`-protected `.evidence/` tree, each bundle keyed to the git
12	branch/commit and the coding-agent session that produced it. A reviewer (or a
13	later agent) opens the bundle's `MANIFEST.md`, watches the demo, and signs off
14	— no re-driving the app.
15	
16	The lifecycle is three scripts: **`new-bundle.sh`** (open a bundle) →
17	**`capture.sh`** (add artifacts, once per surface) → **`finalize.sh`** (stamp a
18	verdict and render the review page). Complements the global `run` / `verify`
19	skills: use *those* to drive the app; use *this* to record what they showed.
20	
21	## When to use
22	
23	- User says "record a demo of this", "leave evidence", "capture a
24	  screenshot/video of the feature", "prove it works", "demos over diffs".
25	- User wants **async 驗收 / sign-off** — they'll review later, not watch you now.
26	- You just finished a feature and want the acceptance artifacts to live
27	  next to the branch/commit that produced them.
28	- A reviewer asked "show me it works" without reading the diff.
29	
30	## When NOT to use
31	
32	- The change has **no runtime surface** (docs, comments, pure refactor with
33	  tests) → nothing to demo; point at the tests.
34	- You just need to *drive* the app to check it yourself → global `run` /
35	  `verify`. Only reach here when you want a **filed, reviewable artifact**.
36	- Posting media **into a PR** → not in v1. `.evidence/` is gitignored, so its
37	  images/videos have no public URL to embed (see Gotchas). Tracked as a `P?`
38	  backlog item.
39	
40	## Workflow
41	
42	### 1. Open a bundle
43	
44	```bash
45	bash skills/local/demo-evidence/scripts/new-bundle.sh \
46	  --title "login flow" --feature "Verify login redirects to /dashboard"
47	# stdout: {"bundle_dir":".evidence/claude-5f932f43/2026-…-6526681-login-flow", ...}
48	```
49	
50	Detects the agent session + git branch/short-SHA/dirty, creates
51	`.evidence/<agent>-<session>/<UTC-ts>-<shortSHA>[-<title>]/`, writes
52	`manifest.json` + a `MANIFEST.md` scaffold, ensures `.evidence/` is gitignored,
53	and records the path in `.evidence/.current`. Later steps default to
54	`.current`, so you rarely pass `--bundle`.
55	
56	### 2. Capture one artifact per surface
57	
58	Pick the mode(s) that fit the app. Each appends to the bundle manifest.
59	
60	```bash
61	CAP="bash skills/local/demo-evidence/scripts/capture.sh"
62	
63	# Web UI — full-page screenshot + video + Playwright trace
64	$CAP web  --url http://localhost:3000/login --name login --steps ./demo-steps.mjs
65	
66	# CLI / TUI — asciinema recording (falls back to a plain tee'd log)
67	$CAP term --cmd "mytool --do-the-thing" --name run
68	
69	# HTTP / API — status + headers + body + timing
70	$CAP http --url http://localhost:8000/health --name health
71	
72	# Desktop / non-browser GUI — timed screen recording
73	$CAP screen --seconds 10 --name walkthrough
74	```
75	
76	Capture what actually demonstrates the feature — don't capture blindly. A
77	before/after screenshot pair or a 10-second flow beats a folder of noise.
78	
79	### 3. Finalize for review
80	
81	```bash
82	bash skills/local/demo-evidence/scripts/finalize.sh \
83	  --verdict PASS \
84	  --step "open /login" --step "submit valid creds" --step "expect /dashboard" \
85	  --scrub
86	```
87	
88	Stamps the verdict, appends reproduction steps, refreshes artifact sizes, runs
89	an optional secret scan, and renders the human-facing `MANIFEST.md` (verdict
90	badge, context, repro steps, artifact table, review checklist). Point the
91	reviewer at `<bundle>/MANIFEST.md`.
92	
93	## Available scripts
94	
95	- **`scripts/new-bundle.sh`** — Create a bundle keyed to session + git; emit its path as JSON. Guarantees `.evidence/` is gitignored.
96	  - Flags: `--title`, `--feature`, `--agent`, `--root`, `--dry-run`, `--help`.
97	  - Exit: `0` ok, `1` bad args, `2` not a git repo, `3` jq missing.
98	- **`scripts/capture.sh <web|term|http|screen>`** — Capture one artifact into a bundle (default `.current`) and record it in `manifest.json`.
99	  - Common: `--bundle`, `--root`, `--name`, `--note`, `--dry-run`.
100	  - `web`: `--url`, `--steps`, `--timeout`. `term`: `--cmd`, `--log`. `http`: `--url`, `--method`, `--data`, `--header` (repeatable). `screen`: `--seconds`, `--device`, `--display`.
101	  - Exit: `0` ok, `1` bad args, `2` no bundle, `3` jq missing, `4` capture tool missing, `5` capture failed.
102	- **`scripts/finalize.sh`** — Set verdict, append steps, refresh sizes, optional secret scan, render `MANIFEST.md`.
103	  - Flags: `--bundle`, `--root`, `--verdict PASS|NEEDS_WORK|pending`, `--step` (repeatable), `--scrub`, `--dry-run`, `--help`.
104	  - Exit: `0` ok, `1` bad args, `2` no bundle, `3` jq missing.
105	- **`scripts/detect-session.sh`** — Best-effort `{agent, session_id, source, specstory_path}` JSON. Standalone or called by `new-bundle.sh`.
106	  - Flags: `--agent`, `--json`/`--tsv`, `--quiet`, `--help`. Exit: `0` always, `1` bad args.
107	
108	## Bundled assets
109	
110	- `assets/capture-web.mjs` — Minimal Playwright runner (screenshot + video +
111	  trace) invoked by `capture.sh web`. Loads `playwright` from the project's
112	  `node_modules` via `createRequire(cwd)`.
113	
114	## Gotchas
115	
116	- **`.evidence/` media has NO public URL — it cannot embed in a GitHub PR.**
117	  The whole point is a gitignored local surface, so images/videos aren't
118	  web-reachable. Posting to a PR (gist-raw-URL image embed, video links) is a
119	  deliberate `P?` backlog item, out of scope for v1. For now, share the bundle
120	  locally or push it out-of-band.
121	- **Screenshots and logs can leak secrets, and screenshots can't be
122	  auto-scrubbed.** `finalize.sh --scrub` only *reports* on text artifacts
123	  (`*.log`, `*.txt`) via gitleaks — a human must eyeball images/video before
124	  sharing them anywhere. Because `.evidence/` is gitignored, nothing reaches
125	  git history, but external sharing is on you.
126	- **`capture.sh web` needs Node + Playwright installed in the project.** If
127	  `playwright` doesn't resolve from the CWD it exits `4` with an install hint
128	  (`npm i -D playwright && npx playwright install chromium`) — or use the
129	  `microsoft/playwright-cli` skill as the browser engine instead.
130	- **`capture.sh screen` on macOS needs Screen Recording permission** and the
131	  right avfoundation device index (default `1`, varies per machine). List
132	  devices with `ffmpeg -f avfoundation -list_devices true -i ""` and pass
133	  `--device`. On Linux it uses `x11grab` on `$DISPLAY`.
134	- **Agent detection is best-effort.** Env markers (`$CLAUDECODE`, `$CURSOR_*`,
135	  `$CODEX_*`) then artifact presence; falls back to `unknown`. Pass
136	  `--agent cursor|codex|…` to `new-bundle.sh` when the session isn't yours.
137	- **`term` falls back to a plain log without asciinema.** The log still
138	  captures stdout+stderr and the command's exit code, but not timing/replay.
139	  Install `asciinema` for a replayable `.cast`.
140	- **Bundles default to `.evidence/.current`.** Running a second `new-bundle.sh`
141	  repoints `.current`; pass `--bundle DIR` to capture into an older bundle.
142
```
</details></tool-use>

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# capture.sh — capture one evidence artifact into a bundle and record it in
3	# the bundle's manifest.json.
4	#
5	#   capture.sh web    --url URL [--steps FILE] [--name N]   (Playwright)
6	#   capture.sh term   --cmd "CMD" [--log] [--name N]        (asciinema / tee)
7	#   capture.sh http   --url URL [--method M] [--data D] ... (curl)
8	#   capture.sh screen [--seconds N] [--device D]            (ffmpeg)
9	#
10	# Bundle defaults to <root>/.current (written by new-bundle.sh). Each mode
11	# preflights its tool and degrades with a clear stderr hint + distinct exit
12	# code, so a missing tool skips one capture without killing the workflow.
13	#
14	# Bash 3.2 compatible (stock macOS).
15	
16	set -euo pipefail
17	
18	usage() {
19	  cat <<'EOF'
20	Usage: capture.sh <web|term|http|screen> [OPTIONS]
21	
22	Capture one artifact into an evidence bundle (see new-bundle.sh) and append
23	it to the bundle's manifest.json.
24	
25	Common options:
26	  --bundle DIR    Target bundle (default: <root>/.current, else newest).
27	  --root DIR      Evidence root used to find .current (default: .evidence).
28	  --name NAME     Artifact base name (default: <mode>-<n>).
29	  --note TEXT     Free-text note stored with the artifact.
30	  --dry-run       Print the capture command; write nothing.
31	  --help, -h      Show this help and exit.
32	
33	web    --url URL [--steps FILE] [--timeout MS]
34	       Playwright: full-page screenshot + video (webm) + trace (zip).
35	term   --cmd "CMD" [--log]
36	       asciinema recording of CMD; --log (or no asciinema) tees a plain log.
37	http   --url URL [--method GET|POST|...] [--data BODY] [--header "K: V"]...
38	       curl: status + headers + body + timing to http/NAME.txt (+ .json).
39	screen [--seconds N] [--device IDX] [--display :0]
40	       ffmpeg screen recording to NAME.mp4 (macOS avfoundation / Linux x11grab).
41	
42	Exit codes:
43	  0  success
44	  1  invalid arguments
45	  2  no usable evidence bundle (run new-bundle.sh first)
46	  3  jq not found
47	  4  capture tool missing (node/playwright, asciinema, curl, or ffmpeg)
48	  5  capture command failed
49	EOF
50	}
51	
52	log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
53	warn() { printf 'warn: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
54	die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
55	
56	HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
57	
58	MODE=""
59	BUNDLE=""
60	ROOT=".evidence"
61	NAME=""
62	NOTE=""
63	DRY_RUN=0
64	# mode-specific
65	URL=""; STEPS=""; TIMEOUT_MS=15000
66	CMD=""; LOG_ONLY=0
67	METHOD="GET"; DATA=""; HEADERS=()
68	SECONDS_REC=8; DEVICE=""; DISPLAY_OVR="${DISPLAY:-:0}"
69	
70	[ $# -gt 0 ] || die "missing mode (web|term|http|screen); try --help" 1
71	case "$1" in

73	  --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
74	  *) die "unknown mode: $1 (expected web|term|http|screen)" 1 ;;
75	esac

77	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do

80	    --bundle)    BUNDLE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;

82	    --root)      ROOT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;

84	    --name)      NAME="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
85	    --note=*)    NOTE="${1#--note=}"; shift ;;
86	    --note)      NOTE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
87	    --url=*)     URL="${1#--url=}"; shift ;;
88	    --url)       URL="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;

1	#!/usr/bin/env node
2	// capture-web.mjs — Playwright capture: full-page screenshot + video + trace.
3	//
4	// Invoked by capture.sh (`capture.sh web`). Loads 'playwright' relative to
5	// process.cwd() via createRequire, so it resolves the *project's* install no
6	// matter where this script lives (it ships inside a skill dir).
7	//
8	// Usage: node capture-web.mjs --url URL --out DIR --name NAME [--steps FILE] [--timeout MS]
9	//   --steps FILE : a JS module that default-exports `async (page) => { ... }`
10	//                  run after navigation (clicks, fills) before the screenshot.
11	// Prints {"screenshot","video","trace"} (names relative to --out) to stdout.
12	
13	import { createRequire } from 'module';
14	import { pathToFileURL } from 'url';
15	import path from 'path';
16	import fs from 'fs';
17	
18	const require = createRequire(process.cwd() + '/');
19	
20	function parseArgs(argv) {
21	  const o = { timeout: 15000 };
22	  for (let i = 0; i < argv.length; i++) {
23	    const a = argv[i];
24	    if (a === '--url') o.url = argv[++i];
25	    else if (a === '--out') o.out = argv[++i];
26	    else if (a === '--name') o.name = argv[++i];
27	    else if (a === '--steps') o.steps = argv[++i];
28	    else if (a === '--timeout') o.timeout = parseInt(argv[++i], 10);
29	    else if (a === '--help' || a === '-h') o.help = true;
30	  }
31	  return o;
32	}
33	
34	const opt = parseArgs(process.argv.slice(2));
35	if (opt.help || !opt.url || !opt.out || !opt.name) {
36	  process.stderr.write(
37	    'usage: capture-web.mjs --url URL --out DIR --name NAME [--steps FILE] [--timeout MS]\n');
38	  process.exit(opt.help ? 0 : 1);
39	}
40	
41	const { chromium } = require('playwright');
42	
43	const shotName = `${opt.name}.png`;
44	const traceName = `${opt.name}-trace.zip`;
45	const videoName = `${opt.name}.webm`;
46	
47	const browser = await chromium.launch();
48	const context = await browser.newContext({ recordVideo: { dir: opt.out } });
49	await context.tracing.start({ screenshots: true, snapshots: true });
50	const page = await context.newPage();
51	
52	let ok = true;
53	try {
54	  await page.goto(opt.url, { waitUntil: 'load', timeout: opt.timeout });
55	  if (opt.steps) {
56	    const mod = await import(pathToFileURL(path.resolve(opt.steps)).href);
57	    if (typeof mod.default === 'function') await mod.default(page);
58	  }
59	  await page.screenshot({ path: path.join(opt.out, shotName), fullPage: true });
60	} catch (e) {
61	  ok = false;
62	  process.stderr.write(`capture-web: ${e.message}\n`);
63	} finally {
64	  await context.tracing.stop({ path: path.join(opt.out, traceName) });
65	  const video = page.video();
66	  await context.close();   // flushes the video file to disk
67	  await browser.close();
68	  if (video) {
69	    try { fs.renameSync(await video.path(), path.join(opt.out, videoName)); }
70	    catch { /* no video on immediate navigation failure */ }
71	  }
72	}
73	
74	const result = {};
75	if (fs.existsSync(path.join(opt.out, shotName))) result.screenshot = shotName;
76	if (fs.existsSync(path.join(opt.out, videoName))) result.video = videoName;
77	if (fs.existsSync(path.join(opt.out, traceName))) result.trace = traceName;
78	process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(result) + '\n');
79	process.exit(ok ? 0 : 5);

111	  log "[dry-run] would create bundle: $BUNDLE_DIR"
112	  log "[dry-run] agent=$AGENT session=$SESSION_ID branch=$BRANCH sha=$SHA dirty=$DIRTY"
113	  printf '{"bundle_dir":"%s","manifest":"%s","agent":"%s","session":"%s","branch":"%s","sha":"%s","dirty":%s,"dry_run":true}\n' \
114	    "$BUNDLE_DIR" "$MANIFEST" "$AGENT" "$SESSION_ID" "$BRANCH" "$SHA" "$DIRTY"
115	  exit 0
116	fi
117	
118	# --- Guarantee the evidence root is gitignored ----------------------------
119	# Idiomatic: a root-anchored entry in the repo's .gitignore (cf. /site, /state/).
120	ROOT_CLEAN="${ROOT#./}"
121	IGNORE_LINE="/$ROOT_CLEAN/"
122	if ! grep -qxF "$IGNORE_LINE" .gitignore 2>/dev/null; then
123	  { printf '\n# demo-evidence: local acceptance artifacts (never committed)\n%s\n' "$IGNORE_LINE"; } >> .gitignore
124	  log "added '$IGNORE_LINE' to .gitignore"
125	fi
126	
127	mkdir -p "$BUNDLE_DIR"
128	if ! git check-ignore -q "$BUNDLE_DIR" 2>/dev/null; then
129	  warn "$BUNDLE_DIR is NOT gitignored — check your .gitignore before committing"
130	fi
131	
132	# --- Write manifest.json ---------------------------------------------------
133	jq -n \
134	  --arg created "$TS_ISO" \
135	  --arg agent   "$AGENT" \
136	  --arg sid     "$SESSION_ID" \
137	  --arg ssrc    "$SESSION_SOURCE" \
138	  --arg spath   "$SPECSTORY_PATH" \
139	  --arg branch  "$BRANCH" \
140	  --arg sha     "$SHA" \
141	  --argjson dirty "$DIRTY" \
142	  --arg title   "$TITLE" \
143	  --arg feature "$FEATURE" \
144	  '{schema:1, created_utc:$created, agent:$agent,
145	    session:{id:$sid, source:$ssrc, specstory_path:$spath},
146	    git:{branch:$branch, sha:$sha, dirty:$dirty},
147	    title:$title, feature:$feature, verdict:"pending",
148	    steps:[], artifacts:[]}' > "$MANIFEST"
149	
150	# --- Write a MANIFEST.md scaffold (finalize.sh renders the real one) ------
151	# Note: printf format strings that begin with '-' must use `printf --`.
152	{
153	  printf '# Evidence: %s\n\n' "${TITLE:-$BUNDLE_NAME}"
154	  printf '> **verdict: pending** — run `finalize.sh --bundle %s --verdict PASS|NEEDS_WORK` when done.\n\n' "$BUNDLE_DIR"
155	  printf -- '- agent/session: `%s` / `%s`\n' "$AGENT" "$SESSION_ID"
156	  printf -- '- git: `%s` @ `%s` (dirty: %s)\n' "$BRANCH" "$SHA" "$DIRTY"
157	  printf -- '- created: `%s`\n\n' "$TS_ISO"
158	  [ -n "$FEATURE" ] && printf '%s\n\n' "$FEATURE"
159	  printf '_No artifacts captured yet._\n'
160	} > "$BUNDLE_DIR/MANIFEST.md"
161	
162	# --- Update the .current pointer (default target for capture.sh) ----------
163	printf '%s\n' "$BUNDLE_DIR" > "$ROOT/.current"
164	
165	log "created bundle: $BUNDLE_DIR"
166	printf '{"bundle_dir":"%s","manifest":"%s","agent":"%s","session":"%s","branch":"%s","sha":"%s","dirty":%s}\n' \
167	  "$BUNDLE_DIR" "$MANIFEST" "$AGENT" "$SESSION_ID" "$BRANCH" "$SHA" "$DIRTY"

 `./skills/local/demo-evidence/scripts/detect-session.sh`

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# detect-session.sh — best-effort identify the current coding-agent session.
3	#
4	# Emits {agent, session_id, source, specstory_path} as JSON (or TSV) so a
5	# caller can key an evidence bundle to the session it was produced in.
6	# Self-contained on purpose: mirrors the core of agent-history-hygiene's
7	# find-session.sh but carries no cross-skill path dependency, so this skill
8	# works when installed on its own.
9	#
10	# Bash 3.2 compatible (stock macOS).
11	
12	set -euo pipefail
13	
14	usage() {
15	  cat <<'EOF'
16	Usage: detect-session.sh [OPTIONS]
17	
18	Best-effort discovery of the coding-agent session for $PWD. Heuristics:
19	  agent      --agent override > env markers ($CLAUDECODE, $CURSOR_*, $CODEX_*)
20	             > artifact presence > "unknown".
21	  session_id Claude session UUID (newest *.jsonl under
22	             ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/, slug = $PWD with '/'->'-'); else the
23	             newest ./.specstory/history/<timestamp>.md timestamp; else
24	             "nosession".
25	
26	Options:
27	  --agent VALUE   Force the agent kind (claude|cursor|codex|...). Skips detection.
28	  --json          Emit JSON to stdout (default).
29	  --tsv           Emit TSV (key<TAB>value per line) instead of JSON.
30	  --quiet         Suppress stderr diagnostics.
31	  --help, -h      Show this help and exit.
32	
33	Output keys: agent, session_id, source, specstory_path
34	
35	Exit codes:
36	  0  always (never fails a pipeline; empty/"unknown" values signal absence).
37	  1  invalid arguments.
38	EOF
39	}
40	
41	log()  { [ "$QUIET" = "1" ] || printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
42	die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
43	
44	AGENT_OVERRIDE=""
45	OUT="json"
46	QUIET=0
47	
48	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
49	  case "$1" in
50	    --agent=*) AGENT_OVERRIDE="${1#--agent=}"; shift ;;
51	    --agent)   AGENT_OVERRIDE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
52	    --json)    OUT="json"; shift ;;
53	    --tsv)     OUT="tsv"; shift ;;
54	    --quiet)   QUIET=1; shift ;;
55	    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
56	    -*)        die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
57	    *)         die "unexpected positional arg: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
58	  esac
59	done
60	
61	# Claude's project slug: absolute $PWD with '/' replaced by '-'.
62	cwd_slug() { printf '%s' "$PWD" | sed 's|/|-|g'; }
63	
64	newest_file() {
65	  # newest_file <dir> <glob> — newest matching file by mtime, or empty.
66	  local dir="$1" glob="$2" found
67	  [ -d "$dir" ] || { printf ''; return 0; }
68	  found=$(find "$dir" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name "$glob" -print0 2>/dev/null \
69	    | xargs -0 ls -t 2>/dev/null \
70	    | head -n 1)
71	  printf '%s' "$found"
72	}
73	
74	# --- Resolve Claude session (UUID + jsonl) --------------------------------
75	CLAUDE_JSONL=""
76	CLAUDE_UUID=""
77	proj_dir="$HOME/.claude/projects/$(cwd_slug)"
78	CLAUDE_JSONL=$(newest_file "$proj_dir" "*.jsonl")
79	[ -n "$CLAUDE_JSONL" ] && CLAUDE_UUID=$(basename "$CLAUDE_JSONL" .jsonl)
80	
81	# --- Resolve SpecStory transcript -----------------------------------------
82	SPECSTORY_PATH=$(newest_file "$PWD/.specstory/history" "*.md")
83	
84	# --- Detect agent kind -----------------------------------------------------
85	# Env markers first (authoritative for the live process), then artifacts.
86	detect_agent() {
87	  if [ -n "$AGENT_OVERRIDE" ]; then printf '%s' "$AGENT_OVERRIDE"; return; fi
88	  if [ -n "${CLAUDECODE:-}" ] || [ -n "${CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT:-}" ]; then
89	    printf 'claude'; return
90	  fi
91	  if [ -n "${CURSOR_TRACE_ID:-}" ] || [ -n "${CURSOR_AGENT:-}" ] || [ -n "${CURSOR_SESSION_ID:-}" ]; then
92	    printf 'cursor'; return
93	  fi
94	  if [ -n "${CODEX_SANDBOX:-}" ] || [ -n "${CODEX_HOME:-}" ] || [ -n "${CODEX_SESSION_ID:-}" ]; then
95	    printf 'codex'; return
96	  fi
97	  # Artifact fallback: a live Claude jsonl for this CWD is a strong signal.
98	  if [ -n "$CLAUDE_UUID" ]; then printf 'claude'; return; fi
99	  printf 'unknown'
100	}
101	AGENT=$(detect_agent)
102	
103	# --- Pick the session id + source -----------------------------------------
104	# Prefer the Claude UUID (stable, unique). Fall back to the SpecStory
105	# timestamp slug (strip any title suffix, keep <date>_<time>Z).
106	SESSION_ID="nosession"
107	SOURCE="none"
108	if [ -n "$CLAUDE_UUID" ]; then
109	  SESSION_ID="$CLAUDE_UUID"
110	  SOURCE="claude_jsonl"
111	elif [ -n "$SPECSTORY_PATH" ]; then
112	  base=$(basename "$SPECSTORY_PATH" .md)
113	  # SpecStory names: <YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SSZ>[-<title-slug>]. Keep the stamp.
114	  SESSION_ID=$(printf '%s' "$base" | sed -E 's/^([0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}_[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}Z).*/\1/')
115	  SOURCE="specstory"
116	fi
117	
118	[ "$AGENT" = "unknown" ] && log "agent kind undetected (pass --agent to override)"
119	[ "$SOURCE" = "none" ]  && log "no Claude jsonl or SpecStory transcript for $PWD"
120	
121	if [ "$OUT" = "tsv" ]; then
122	  printf 'agent\t%s\n'          "$AGENT"
123	  printf 'session_id\t%s\n'     "$SESSION_ID"
124	  printf 'source\t%s\n'         "$SOURCE"
125	  printf 'specstory_path\t%s\n' "$SPECSTORY_PATH"
126	else
127	  printf '{"agent":"%s","session_id":"%s","source":"%s","specstory_path":"%s"}\n' \
128	    "$AGENT" "$SESSION_ID" "$SOURCE" "$SPECSTORY_PATH"
129	fi
130

4	#

6	#   capture.sh term   --cmd "CMD" [--log] [--name N]        (asciinema / tee)
7	#   capture.sh http   --url URL [--method M] [--data D] ... (curl)
8	#   capture.sh screen [--seconds N] [--device D]            (ffmpeg)
9	#
10	# Bundle defaults to <root>/.current (written by new-bundle.sh). Each mode
11	# preflights its tool and degrades with a clear stderr hint + distinct exit
12	# code, so a missing tool skips one capture without killing the workflow.
13	#
14	# Bash 3.2 compatible (stock macOS).

22	Capture one artifact into an evidence bundle (see new-bundle.sh) and append
23	it to the bundle's manifest.json.
24	
25	Common options:
26	  --bundle DIR    Target bundle (default: <root>/.current, else newest).
27	  --root DIR      Evidence root used to find .current (default: .evidence).
28	  --name NAME     Artifact base name (default: <mode>-<n>).
29	  --note TEXT     Free-text note stored with the artifact.
30	  --dry-run       Print the capture command; write nothing.
31	  --help, -h      Show this help and exit.
32	
33	web    --url URL [--steps FILE] [--timeout MS]
34	       Playwright: full-page screenshot + video (webm) + trace (zip).
35	term   --cmd "CMD" [--log]
36	       asciinema recording of CMD; --log (or no asciinema) tees a plain log.
37	http   --url URL [--method GET|POST|...] [--data BODY] [--header "K: V"]...
38	       curl: status + headers + body + timing to http/NAME.txt (+ .json).
39	screen [--seconds N] [--device IDX] [--display :0]
40	       ffmpeg screen recording to NAME.mp4 (macOS avfoundation / Linux x11grab).
41

240	  local out="$BUNDLE/$NAME.mp4" os; os="$(uname -s)"
241	  local ff=(ffmpeg -y -t "$SECONDS_REC")
242	  if [ "$os" = "Darwin" ]; then
243	    local dev="${DEVICE:-1}"   # avfoundation screen index; varies per machine
244	    ff+=(-f avfoundation -i "$dev:none")
245	    log "macOS: recording avfoundation device '$dev' — needs Screen Recording permission."
246	    log "  list devices: ffmpeg -f avfoundation -list_devices true -i \"\""
247	  else

249	  fi

251	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then log "[dry-run] ${ff[*]}"; return 0; fi
252	  "${ff[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "ffmpeg screen capture failed (check device/permission)" 5
253	  add_artifact "$NAME.mp4" video ffmpeg "$out" "$NOTE"
254	}
255	
256	case "$MODE" in
257	  web)    capture_web ;;
258	  term)   capture_term ;;
259	  http)   capture_http ;;
260	  screen) capture_screen ;;

2	# detect-session.sh — best-effort identify the current coding-agent session.
3	#
4	# Emits {agent, session_id, source, specstory_path} as JSON (or TSV) so a
5	# caller can key an evidence bundle to the session it was produced in.
6	# Self-contained on purpose: mirrors the core of agent-history-hygiene's

8	# works when installed on its own.
9	#

11	
12	set -euo pipefail
13	
14	usage() {
15	  cat <<'EOF'
16	Usage: detect-session.sh [OPTIONS]
17	
18	Best-effort discovery of the coding-agent session for $PWD. Heuristics:
19	  agent      --agent override > env markers ($CLAUDECODE, $CURSOR_*, $CODEX_*)
20	             > artifact presence > "unknown".
21	  session_id Claude session UUID (newest *.jsonl under
22	             ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/, slug = $PWD with '/'->'-'); else the
23	             newest ./.specstory/history/<timestamp>.md timestamp; else
24	             "nosession".
25	
26	Options:
27	  --agent VALUE   Force the agent kind (claude|cursor|codex|...). Skips detection.
28	  --json          Emit JSON to stdout (default).
29	  --tsv           Emit TSV (key<TAB>value per line) instead of JSON.
30	  --quiet         Suppress stderr diagnostics.
31	  --help, -h      Show this help and exit.
32	
33	Output keys: agent, session_id, source, specstory_path
34	
35	Exit codes:
36	  0  always (never fails a pipeline; empty/"unknown" values signal absence).
37	  1  invalid arguments.
38	EOF
39	}
40	
41	log()  { [ "$QUIET" = "1" ] || printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
42	die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
43	
44	AGENT_OVERRIDE=""
45	OUT="json"
46	QUIET=0
47	
48	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
49	  case "$1" in
50	    --agent=*) AGENT_OVERRIDE="${1#--agent=}"; shift ;;
51	    --agent)   AGENT_OVERRIDE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
52	    --json)    OUT="json"; shift ;;
53	    --tsv)     OUT="tsv"; shift ;;
54	    --quiet)   QUIET=1; shift ;;
55	    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
56	    -*)        die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
57	    *)         die "unexpected positional arg: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
58	  esac
59	done
60	
61	# Claude's project slug: absolute $PWD with '/' replaced by '-'.
62	cwd_slug() { printf '%s' "$PWD" | sed 's|/|-|g'; }
63	
64	newest_file() {
65	  # newest_file <dir> <glob> — newest matching file by mtime, or empty.
66	  local dir="$1" glob="$2" found
67	  [ -d "$dir" ] || { printf ''; return 0; }
68	  found=$(find "$dir" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name "$glob" -print0 2>/dev/null \
69	    | xargs -0 ls -t 2>/dev/null \
70	    | head -n 1)
71	  printf '%s' "$found"
72	}
73	
74	# --- Resolve Claude session (UUID + jsonl) --------------------------------
75	CLAUDE_JSONL=""
76	CLAUDE_UUID=""
77	proj_dir="$HOME/.claude/projects/$(cwd_slug)"
78	CLAUDE_JSONL=$(newest_file "$proj_dir" "*.jsonl")

89	    printf 'claude'; return

92	    printf 'cursor'; return

95	    printf 'codex'; return

114	  SESSION_ID=$(printf '%s' "$base" | sed -E 's/^([0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}_[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}Z).*/\1/')
115	  SOURCE="specstory"

119	[ "$SOURCE" = "none" ]  && log "no Claude jsonl or SpecStory transcript for $PWD"
120	
121	if [ "$OUT" = "tsv" ]; then
122	  printf 'agent\t%s\n'          "$AGENT"
123	  printf 'session_id\t%s\n'     "$SESSION_ID"
124	  printf 'source\t%s\n'         "$SOURCE"
125	  printf 'specstory_path\t%s\n' "$SPECSTORY_PATH"
126	else
127	  printf '{"agent":"%s","session_id":"%s","source":"%s","specstory_path":"%s"}\n' \
128	    "$AGENT" "$SESSION_ID" "$SOURCE" "$SPECSTORY_PATH"
129	fi

2	# capture.sh — capture one evidence artifact into a bundle and record it in
3	# the bundle's manifest.json.
4	#
5	#   capture.sh web    --url URL [--steps FILE] [--name N]   (Playwright)
6	#   capture.sh term   --cmd "CMD" [--log] [--name N]        (asciinema / tee)
7	#   capture.sh http   --url URL [--method M] [--data D] ... (curl)
8	#   capture.sh screen [--seconds N] [--device D]            (ffmpeg)
9	#
10	# Bundle defaults to <root>/.current (written by new-bundle.sh). Each mode
11	# preflights its tool and degrades with a clear stderr hint + distinct exit
12	# code, so a missing tool skips one capture without killing the workflow.
13	#
14	# Bash 3.2 compatible (stock macOS).
15	
16	set -euo pipefail
17	
18	usage() {
19	  cat <<'EOF'
20	Usage: capture.sh <web|term|http|screen> [OPTIONS]
21	
22	Capture one artifact into an evidence bundle (see new-bundle.sh) and append
23	it to the bundle's manifest.json.
24	
25	Common options:
26	  --bundle DIR    Target bundle (default: <root>/.current, else newest).
27	  --root DIR      Evidence root used to find .current (default: .evidence).
28	  --name NAME     Artifact base name (default: <mode>-<n>).
29	  --note TEXT     Free-text note stored with the artifact.
30	  --dry-run       Print the capture command; write nothing.
31	  --help, -h      Show this help and exit.
32	
33	web    --url URL [--steps FILE] [--timeout MS]
34	       Playwright: full-page screenshot + video (webm) + trace (zip).
35	term   --cmd "CMD" [--log]
36	       asciinema recording of CMD; --log (or no asciinema) tees a plain log.
37	http   --url URL [--method GET|POST|...] [--data BODY] [--header "K: V"]...
38	       curl: status + headers + body + timing to http/NAME.txt (+ .json).
39	screen [--seconds N] [--device IDX] [--display :0]
40	       ffmpeg screen recording to NAME.mp4 (macOS avfoundation / Linux x11grab).
41	
42	Exit codes:
43	  0  success
44	  1  invalid arguments
45	  2  no usable evidence bundle (run new-bundle.sh first)
46	  3  jq not found
47	  4  capture tool missing (node/playwright, asciinema, curl, or ffmpeg)
48	  5  capture command failed
49	EOF
50	}
51	
52	log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
53	warn() { printf 'warn: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
54	die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
55	
56	HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
57	
58	MODE=""
59	BUNDLE=""
60	ROOT=".evidence"
61	NAME=""
62	NOTE=""
63	DRY_RUN=0
64	# mode-specific
65	URL=""; STEPS=""; TIMEOUT_MS=15000
66	CMD=""; LOG_ONLY=0
67	METHOD="GET"; DATA=""; HEADERS=()
68	SECONDS_REC=8; DEVICE=""; DISPLAY_OVR="${DISPLAY:-:0}"
69	
70	[ $# -gt 0 ] || die "missing mode (web|term|http|screen); try --help" 1
71	case "$1" in
72	  web|term|http|screen) MODE="$1"; shift ;;
73	  --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
74	  *) die "unknown mode: $1 (expected web|term|http|screen)" 1 ;;
75	esac
76	
77	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
78	  case "$1" in
79	    --bundle=*)  BUNDLE="${1#--bundle=}"; shift ;;
80	    --bundle)    BUNDLE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
81	    --root=*)    ROOT="${1#--root=}"; shift ;;
82	    --root)      ROOT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
83	    --name=*)    NAME="${1#--name=}"; shift ;;
84	    --name)      NAME="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
85	    --note=*)    NOTE="${1#--note=}"; shift ;;
86	    --note)      NOTE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
87	    --url=*)     URL="${1#--url=}"; shift ;;
88	    --url)       URL="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
89	    --steps=*)   STEPS="${1#--steps=}"; shift ;;
90	    --steps)     STEPS="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
91	    --timeout=*) TIMEOUT_MS="${1#--timeout=}"; shift ;;
92	    --timeout)   TIMEOUT_MS="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
93	    --cmd=*)     CMD="${1#--cmd=}"; shift ;;
94	    --cmd)       CMD="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
95	    --log)       LOG_ONLY=1; shift ;;
96	    --method=*)  METHOD="${1#--method=}"; shift ;;
97	    --method)    METHOD="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
98	    --data=*)    DATA="${1#--data=}"; shift ;;
99	    --data)      DATA="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
100	    --header=*)  HEADERS+=("${1#--header=}"); shift ;;
101	    --header)    HEADERS+=("${2:-}"); shift 2 ;;
102	    --seconds=*) SECONDS_REC="${1#--seconds=}"; shift ;;
103	    --seconds)   SECONDS_REC="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
104	    --device=*)  DEVICE="${1#--device=}"; shift ;;
105	    --device)    DEVICE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
106	    --display=*) DISPLAY_OVR="${1#--display=}"; shift ;;
107	    --display)   DISPLAY_OVR="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
108	    --dry-run)   DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
109	    --help|-h)   usage; exit 0 ;;
110	    -*)          die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
111	    *)           die "unexpected positional arg: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
112	  esac
113	done
114	
115	command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "jq not found in PATH (install: brew install jq)" 3
116	
117	# Anchor at repo top level so relative --root resolves consistently.
118	if git rev-parse --show-toplevel >/dev/null 2>&1; then
119	  cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
120	fi
121	
122	# --- Resolve target bundle -------------------------------------------------
123	if [ -z "$BUNDLE" ]; then
124	  if [ -f "$ROOT/.current" ]; then
125	    BUNDLE="$(head -n1 "$ROOT/.current")"
126	  else
127	    BUNDLE="$(find "$ROOT" -type f -name manifest.json -print0 2>/dev/null \
128	      | xargs -0 ls -t 2>/dev/null | head -n1 | sed 's|/manifest.json$||')"
129	  fi
130	fi
131	[ -n "$BUNDLE" ] && [ -f "$BUNDLE/manifest.json" ] \
132	  || die "no evidence bundle found (run new-bundle.sh first)" 2
133	MANIFEST="$BUNDLE/manifest.json"
134	
135	# Default artifact name: <mode>-<n> where n = existing artifact count + 1.
136	if [ -z "$NAME" ]; then
137	  n=$(jq '.artifacts | length' "$MANIFEST")
138	  NAME="$MODE-$((n + 1))"
139	fi
140	
141	# add_artifact <name> <kind> <tool> <path-for-size> <note>
142	add_artifact() {
143	  local n="$1" kind="$2" tool="$3" path="$4" note="$5" bytes=0 tmp
144	  [ -f "$path" ] && bytes=$(wc -c < "$path" | tr -d ' ')
145	  tmp="$(mktemp)"
146	  jq --arg n "$n" --arg k "$kind" --arg t "$tool" \
147	     --argjson b "${bytes:-0}" --arg note "$note" \
148	     '.artifacts += [{name:$n, kind:$k, tool:$t, bytes:$b, note:$note}]' \
149	     "$MANIFEST" > "$tmp" && mv "$tmp" "$MANIFEST"
150	  log "recorded artifact: $n ($kind, ${bytes:-0} bytes)"
151	}
152	
153	# ==========================================================================
154	capture_web() {
155	  [ -n "$URL" ] || die "web mode requires --url" 1
156	  local mjs="$HERE/../assets/capture-web.mjs"
157	  [ -f "$mjs" ] || die "missing $mjs" 4
158	  command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "node not found — install Node.js, or use the microsoft/playwright-cli skill" 4
159	  node -e "require('module').createRequire(process.cwd()+'/').resolve('playwright')" 2>/dev/null \
160	    || die "playwright not resolvable from $(pwd) — run: npm i -D playwright && npx playwright install chromium (or use the microsoft/playwright-cli skill)" 4
161	
162	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
163	    log "[dry-run] node $mjs --url $URL --out $BUNDLE --name $NAME ${STEPS:+--steps $STEPS}"
164	    return 0
165	  fi
166	  local out_json
167	  out_json="$(node "$mjs" --url "$URL" --out "$BUNDLE" --name "$NAME" \
168	    --timeout "$TIMEOUT_MS" ${STEPS:+--steps "$STEPS"})" \
169	    || die "capture-web.mjs failed for $URL" 5
170	  # mjs prints {"screenshot":"..","video":"..","trace":".."} (relative to bundle)
171	  local shot vid trace
172	  shot="$(printf '%s' "$out_json" | jq -r '.screenshot // empty')"
173	  vid="$(printf '%s' "$out_json" | jq -r '.video // empty')"
174	  trace="$(printf '%s' "$out_json" | jq -r '.trace // empty')"
175	  [ -n "$shot" ]  && add_artifact "$shot"  screenshot playwright "$BUNDLE/$shot"  "$NOTE"
176	  [ -n "$vid" ]   && add_artifact "$vid"   video      playwright "$BUNDLE/$vid"   "$NOTE"
177	  [ -n "$trace" ] && add_artifact "$trace" trace      playwright "$BUNDLE/$trace" "$NOTE"
178	}
179	
180	capture_term() {
181	  [ -n "$CMD" ] || die "term mode requires --cmd" 1
182	  local have_asciinema=0
183	  command -v asciinema >/dev/null 2>&1 && have_asciinema=1
184	
185	  if [ "$LOG_ONLY" = "0" ] && [ "$have_asciinema" = "1" ]; then
186	    local out="$BUNDLE/$NAME.cast"
187	    if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then log "[dry-run] asciinema rec -c \"$CMD\" $out"; return 0; fi
188	    asciinema rec --overwrite -c "$CMD" "$out" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
189	      || die "asciinema recording failed" 5
190	    add_artifact "$NAME.cast" asciicast asciinema "$out" "$NOTE"
191	  else
192	    [ "$have_asciinema" = "1" ] || log "asciinema not found — falling back to plain log"
193	    local out="$BUNDLE/$NAME.log"
194	    if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then log "[dry-run] tee log of: $CMD -> $out"; return 0; fi
195	    {
196	      printf '$ %s\n\n' "$CMD"
197	      set +e
198	      bash -c "$CMD" 2>&1
199	      rc=$?
200	      set -e
201	      printf '\n[exit %s]\n' "$rc"
202	    } | tee "$out" >/dev/null
203	    add_artifact "$NAME.log" log tee "$out" "$NOTE"
204	  fi
205	}
206	
207	capture_http() {
208	  [ -n "$URL" ] || die "http mode requires --url" 1
209	  command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "curl not found in PATH" 4
210	  mkdir -p "$BUNDLE/http"
211	  local body="$BUNDLE/http/$NAME.body" hdr="$BUNDLE/http/$NAME.headers"
212	  local txt="$BUNDLE/http/$NAME.txt" sj="$BUNDLE/http/$NAME.json"
213	  local curl_args=(-sS -X "$METHOD" -D "$hdr" -o "$body"
214	                   -w '%{http_code}\t%{time_total}\t%{size_download}')
215	  local h; for h in "${HEADERS[@]:-}"; do [ -n "$h" ] && curl_args+=(-H "$h"); done
216	  [ -n "$DATA" ] && curl_args+=(--data "$DATA")
217	
218	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then log "[dry-run] curl ${curl_args[*]} $URL"; return 0; fi
219	  local meta status time_total size_dl
220	  meta="$(curl "${curl_args[@]}" "$URL")" || die "curl failed for $URL" 5
221	  status="$(printf '%s' "$meta" | cut -f1)"
222	  time_total="$(printf '%s' "$meta" | cut -f2)"
223	  size_dl="$(printf '%s' "$meta" | cut -f3)"
224	  {
225	    printf '%s %s\n\n' "$METHOD" "$URL"
226	    printf '=== response headers ===\n'; cat "$hdr"
227	    printf '\n=== body ===\n'; cat "$body"
228	  } > "$txt"
229	  jq -n --arg url "$URL" --arg method "$METHOD" --arg status "$status" \
230	        --arg time "$time_total" --arg bytes "$size_dl" \
231	        '{url:$url, method:$method, status:($status|tonumber?), time_total:($time|tonumber?), bytes:($bytes|tonumber?)}' \
232	        > "$sj"
233	  rm -f "$hdr" "$body"
234	  log "http $METHOD $URL -> $status (${time_total}s)"
235	  add_artifact "http/$NAME.txt" http curl "$txt" "$NOTE status=$status"
236	}
237	
238	capture_screen() {
239	  command -v ffmpeg >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "ffmpeg not found in PATH (install: brew install ffmpeg)" 4
240	  local out="$BUNDLE/$NAME.mp4" os; os="$(uname -s)"
241	  local ff=(ffmpeg -y -t "$SECONDS_REC")
242	  if [ "$os" = "Darwin" ]; then
243	    local dev="${DEVICE:-1}"   # avfoundation screen index; varies per machine
244	    ff+=(-f avfoundation -i "$dev:none")
245	    log "macOS: recording avfoundation device '$dev' — needs Screen Recording permission."
246	    log "  list devices: ffmpeg -f avfoundation -list_devices true -i \"\""
247	  else
248	    ff+=(-f x11grab -i "$DISPLAY_OVR")
249	  fi
250	  ff+=("$out")
251	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then log "[dry-run] ${ff[*]}"; return 0; fi
252	  "${ff[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "ffmpeg screen capture failed (check device/permission)" 5
253	  add_artifact "$NAME.mp4" video ffmpeg "$out" "$NOTE"
254	}
255	
256	case "$MODE" in
257	  web)    capture_web ;;
258	  term)   capture_term ;;
259	  http)   capture_http ;;
260	  screen) capture_screen ;;
261	esac

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# detect-session.sh — best-effort identify the current coding-agent session.
3	#
4	# Emits {agent, session_id, source, specstory_path} as JSON (or TSV) so a
5	# caller can key an evidence bundle to the session it was produced in.
6	# Self-contained on purpose: mirrors the core of agent-history-hygiene's
7	# find-session.sh but carries no cross-skill path dependency, so this skill
8	# works when installed on its own.
9	#
10	# Bash 3.2 compatible (stock macOS).
11	
12	set -euo pipefail
13	
14	usage() {
15	  cat <<'EOF'
16	Usage: detect-session.sh [OPTIONS]
17	
18	Best-effort discovery of the coding-agent session for $PWD. Heuristics:
19	  agent      --agent override > env markers ($CLAUDECODE, $CURSOR_*, $CODEX_*)
20	             > artifact presence > "unknown".
21	  session_id Claude session UUID (newest *.jsonl under
22	             ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/, slug = $PWD with '/'->'-'); else the
23	             newest ./.specstory/history/<timestamp>.md timestamp; else
24	             "nosession".
25	
26	Options:
27	  --agent VALUE   Force the agent kind (claude|cursor|codex|...). Skips detection.
28	  --json          Emit JSON to stdout (default).
29	  --tsv           Emit TSV (key<TAB>value per line) instead of JSON.
30	  --quiet         Suppress stderr diagnostics.
31	  --help, -h      Show this help and exit.
32	
33	Output keys: agent, session_id, source, specstory_path
34	
35	Exit codes:
36	  0  always (never fails a pipeline; empty/"unknown" values signal absence).
37	  1  invalid arguments.
38	EOF
39	}
40	
41	log()  { [ "$QUIET" = "1" ] || printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
42	die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
43	
44	AGENT_OVERRIDE=""
45	OUT="json"
46	QUIET=0
47	
48	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
49	  case "$1" in
50	    --agent=*) AGENT_OVERRIDE="${1#--agent=}"; shift ;;
51	    --agent)   AGENT_OVERRIDE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
52	    --json)    OUT="json"; shift ;;
53	    --tsv)     OUT="tsv"; shift ;;
54	    --quiet)   QUIET=1; shift ;;
55	    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
56	    -*)        die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
57	    *)         die "unexpected positional arg: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
58	  esac
59	done
60	
61	# Claude's project slug: absolute $PWD with '/' replaced by '-'.
62	cwd_slug() { printf '%s' "$PWD" | sed 's|/|-|g'; }
63	
64	newest_file() {
65	  # newest_file <dir> <glob> — newest matching file by mtime, or empty.
66	  local dir="$1" glob="$2" found
67	  [ -d "$dir" ] || { printf ''; return 0; }
68	  found=$(find "$dir" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name "$glob" -print0 2>/dev/null \
69	    | xargs -0 ls -t 2>/dev/null \
70	    | head -n 1)
71	  printf '%s' "$found"
72	}
73	
74	# --- Resolve Claude session (UUID + jsonl) --------------------------------
75	CLAUDE_JSONL=""
76	CLAUDE_UUID=""
77	proj_dir="$HOME/.claude/projects/$(cwd_slug)"
78	CLAUDE_JSONL=$(newest_file "$proj_dir" "*.jsonl")
79	[ -n "$CLAUDE_JSONL" ] && CLAUDE_UUID=$(basename "$CLAUDE_JSONL" .jsonl)
80	
81	# --- Resolve SpecStory transcript -----------------------------------------
82	SPECSTORY_PATH=$(newest_file "$PWD/.specstory/history" "*.md")
83	
84	# --- Detect agent kind -----------------------------------------------------
85	# Env markers first (authoritative for the live process), then artifacts.
86	detect_agent() {
87	  if [ -n "$AGENT_OVERRIDE" ]; then printf '%s' "$AGENT_OVERRIDE"; return; fi
88	  if [ -n "${CLAUDECODE:-}" ] || [ -n "${CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT:-}" ]; then
89	    printf 'claude'; return
90	  fi
91	  if [ -n "${CURSOR_TRACE_ID:-}" ] || [ -n "${CURSOR_AGENT:-}" ] || [ -n "${CURSOR_SESSION_ID:-}" ]; then
92	    printf 'cursor'; return
93	  fi
94	  if [ -n "${CODEX_SANDBOX:-}" ] || [ -n "${CODEX_HOME:-}" ] || [ -n "${CODEX_SESSION_ID:-}" ]; then
95	    printf 'codex'; return
96	  fi
97	  # Artifact fallback: a live Claude jsonl for this CWD is a strong signal.
98	  if [ -n "$CLAUDE_UUID" ]; then printf 'claude'; return; fi
99	  printf 'unknown'
100	}
101	AGENT=$(detect_agent)
102	
103	# --- Pick the session id + source -----------------------------------------
104	# Prefer the Claude UUID (stable, unique). Fall back to the SpecStory
105	# timestamp slug (strip any title suffix, keep <date>_<time>Z).
106	SESSION_ID="nosession"
107	SOURCE="none"
108	if [ -n "$CLAUDE_UUID" ]; then
109	  SESSION_ID="$CLAUDE_UUID"
110	  SOURCE="claude_jsonl"
111	elif [ -n "$SPECSTORY_PATH" ]; then
112	  base=$(basename "$SPECSTORY_PATH" .md)
113	  # SpecStory names: <YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SSZ>[-<title-slug>]. Keep the stamp.
114	  SESSION_ID=$(printf '%s' "$base" | sed -E 's/^([0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}_[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}Z).*/\1/')
115	  SOURCE="specstory"
116	fi
117	
118	[ "$AGENT" = "unknown" ] && log "agent kind undetected (pass --agent to override)"
119	[ "$SOURCE" = "none" ]  && log "no Claude jsonl or SpecStory transcript for $PWD"
120	
121	if [ "$OUT" = "tsv" ]; then
122	  printf 'agent\t%s\n'          "$AGENT"
123	  printf 'session_id\t%s\n'     "$SESSION_ID"
124	  printf 'source\t%s\n'         "$SOURCE"
125	  printf 'specstory_path\t%s\n' "$SPECSTORY_PATH"
126	else
127	  printf '{"agent":"%s","session_id":"%s","source":"%s","specstory_path":"%s"}\n' \
128	    "$AGENT" "$SESSION_ID" "$SOURCE" "$SPECSTORY_PATH"
129	fi

But when using the specstory fallback, the session ID becomes the full timestamp-plus-title slug. The detect-session.sh script is supposed to strip the title and keep only the timestamp portion like `2025-07-18_01-25Z`, but the real manifest shows the session ID still includes the full title suffix, which creates much longer directory names than the doc example suggests.

Looking closer at the regex pattern in detect-session.sh, it expects the timestamp format `YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SSZ` with seconds, but the actual specstory filenames use `YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MMZ` without seconds. <think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Now I'm doing an adversarial audit of the script to catch potential issues. The verdict validation looks solid—it checks for PASS, NEEDS_WORK, or pending and is case-sensitive, which is fine. But I'm noticing the `--step` append operation always adds to the steps array, so re-running finalize.sh with the same step would create duplicates instead of being idempotent.

This is a real robustness concern since finalize is meant to be re-run to refresh sizes and re-render, so if someone calls it again with `--step`, they'd accumulate duplicate entries. The size refresh logic iterates through artifacts and updates bytes using `wc -c`, defaulting to 0 for missing files, which handles the nested paths correctly and matches the actual file sizes. Now looking at the git handling...

The gitleaks invocation uses `gitleaks stdin` to read from stdin with `--no-banner`, which is a valid command. The exit code logic treats non-zero as leaks found, though this could misreport actual errors as secrets. The scrub only scans `.log` and `.txt` files, so the bookings file gets checked but the manifest doesn't, which is fine since it's report-only anyway — the help text confirms it doesn't actually scrub, just reports, so the naming is a bit misleading but consistent with the documentation.

Now checking the MANIFEST.md rendering...

Generating markdown table...

The artifact names are used directly as link URLs without encoding, which could break if they contained spaces or special characters—though none are present here. The heredoc approach for reading artifact names into the while loop avoids stdin conflicts since jq reads from the temporary file directly. The real issue to focus on is the `--step` idempotency behavior.

The script is designed to be re-run for updates, but if you pass the same steps via `--step` multiple times, they get appended rather than replaced. This matters in the typical workflow where you might finalize once with NEEDS_WORK, then again with PASS—both times passing steps would create duplicates. There's also a minor UX gap where the verdict validation rejects lowercase "pass" even though the help text inconsistently shows "pending" in lowercase. The JSON construction on line 205 shell-interpolates the BUNDLE path directly into the jq filter string, which could theoretically cause injection if the path contained quotes or backslashes—using `--arg` would be safer. The dry-run behavior with refresh needs checking too.

When gitleaks finds secrets, the scrub warning prints once; when it doesn't find any, the warning prints at a different line—both are fine. A more subtle robustness gap: if an artifact listed in the manifest is missing from disk, `refresh_sizes` silently sets its size to 0 with no warning, so a deleted file would just show "0 B" with a broken link. The badge logic for NEEDS_WORK and pending looks correct. The heredoc handling for empty artifact names and the STEPS array expansion with `set -u` both work as intended. Now I'm ranking these findings by severity to finalize the analysis. I'm reconsidering the severity of the step idempotency issue — the help text says --step is "repeatable," but if finalize.sh is re-run (which is the whole point of a finalize script that renders), and the user's invocation script always passes --step, they'll end up duplicating steps. That's a real robustness concern even if it requires the user to re-pass the flag. I'll mark it as such and write up the findings now.
</details></think>

---

# demo evidence

Reviewing an agent's work usually means reading the diff or booting the app
by hand. This skill has the agent **leave behind acceptance evidence** —
screenshots, screen/terminal recordings, request logs — filed into a
`.gitignore`-protected `.evidence/` tree, each bundle keyed to the git
branch/commit and the coding-agent session that produced it. A reviewer (or a
later agent) opens the bundle's `MANIFEST.md`, watches the demo, and signs off
— no re-driving the app.

The lifecycle is three scripts: **`new-bundle.sh`** (open a bundle) →
**`capture.sh`** (add artifacts, once per surface) → **`finalize.sh`** (stamp a
verdict and render the review page). Complements the global `run` / `verify`
skills: use *those* to drive the app; use *this* to record what they showed.

## When to use

- User says "record a demo of this", "leave evidence", "capture a
  screenshot/video of the feature", "prove it works", "demos over diffs".
- User wants **async 驗收 / sign-off** — they'll review later, not watch you now.
- You just finished a feature and want the acceptance artifacts to live
  next to the branch/commit that produced them.
- A reviewer asked "show me it works" without reading the diff.

## When NOT to use

- The change has **no runtime surface** (docs, comments, pure refactor with
  tests) → nothing to demo; point at the tests.
- You just need to *drive* the app to check it yourself → global `run` /
  `verify`. Only reach here when you want a **filed, reviewable artifact**.
- Posting media **into a PR** → not in v1. `.evidence/` is gitignored, so its
  images/videos have no public URL to embed (see Gotchas). Tracked as a `P?`
  backlog item.

## Workflow

### 1. Open a bundle

```bash
bash skills/local/demo-evidence/scripts/new-bundle.sh \
  --title "login flow" --feature "Verify login redirects to /dashboard"
# stdout: {"bundle_dir":".evidence/claude-5f932f43/2026-…-6526681-login-flow", ...}
```

Detects the agent session + git branch/short-SHA/dirty, creates
`.evidence/<agent>-<session>/<UTC-ts>-<shortSHA>[-<title>]/`, writes
`manifest.json` + a `MANIFEST.md` scaffold, ensures `.evidence/` is gitignored,
and records the path in `.evidence/.current`. Later steps default to
`.current`, so you rarely pass `--bundle`.

### 2. Capture one artifact per surface

Pick the mode(s) that fit the app. Each appends to the bundle manifest.

```bash
CAP="bash skills/local/demo-evidence/scripts/capture.sh"

# Web UI — full-page screenshot + video + Playwright trace
$CAP web  --url http://localhost:3000/login --name login --steps ./demo-steps.mjs

# CLI / TUI — asciinema recording (falls back to a plain tee'd log)
$CAP term --cmd "mytool --do-the-thing" --name run

# HTTP / API — status + headers + body + timing
$CAP http --url http://localhost:8000/health --name health

# Desktop / non-browser GUI — timed screen recording
$CAP screen --seconds 10 --name walkthrough
```

Capture what actually demonstrates the feature — don't capture blindly. A
before/after screenshot pair or a 10-second flow beats a folder of noise.

### 3. Finalize for review

```bash
bash skills/local/demo-evidence/scripts/finalize.sh \
  --verdict PASS \
  --step "open /login" --step "submit valid creds" --step "expect /dashboard" \
  --scrub
```

Stamps the verdict, appends reproduction steps, refreshes artifact sizes, runs
an optional secret scan, and renders the human-facing `MANIFEST.md` (verdict
badge, context, repro steps, artifact table, review checklist). Point the
reviewer at `<bundle>/MANIFEST.md`.

## Available scripts

- **`scripts/new-bundle.sh`** — Create a bundle keyed to session + git; emit its path as JSON. Guarantees `.evidence/` is gitignored.
  - Flags: `--title`, `--feature`, `--agent`, `--root`, `--dry-run`, `--help`.
  - Exit: `0` ok, `1` bad args, `2` not a git repo, `3` jq missing.
- **`scripts/capture.sh <web|term|http|screen>`** — Capture one artifact into a bundle (default `.current`) and record it in `manifest.json`.
  - Common: `--bundle`, `--root`, `--name`, `--note`, `--dry-run`.
  - `web`: `--url`, `--steps`, `--timeout`. `term`: `--cmd`, `--log`. `http`: `--url`, `--method`, `--data`, `--header` (repeatable). `screen`: `--seconds`, `--device`, `--display`.
  - Exit: `0` ok, `1` bad args, `2` no bundle, `3` jq missing, `4` capture tool missing, `5` capture failed.
- **`scripts/finalize.sh`** — Set verdict, append steps, refresh sizes, optional secret scan, render `MANIFEST.md`.
  - Flags: `--bundle`, `--root`, `--verdict PASS|NEEDS_WORK|pending`, `--step` (repeatable), `--scrub`, `--dry-run`, `--help`.
  - Exit: `0` ok, `1` bad args, `2` no bundle, `3` jq missing.
- **`scripts/detect-session.sh`** — Best-effort `{agent, session_id, source, specstory_path}` JSON. Standalone or called by `new-bundle.sh`.
  - Flags: `--agent`, `--json`/`--tsv`, `--quiet`, `--help`. Exit: `0` always, `1` bad args.

## Bundled assets

- `assets/capture-web.mjs` — Minimal Playwright runner (screenshot + video +
  trace) invoked by `capture.sh web`. Loads `playwright` from the project's
  `node_modules` via `createRequire(cwd)`.

## Gotchas

- **`.evidence/` media has NO public URL — it cannot embed in a GitHub PR.**
  The whole point is a gitignored local surface, so images/videos aren't
  web-reachable. Posting to a PR (gist-raw-URL image embed, video links) is a
  deliberate `P?` backlog item, out of scope for v1. For now, share the bundle
  locally or push it out-of-band.
- **Screenshots and logs can leak secrets, and screenshots can't be
  auto-scrubbed.** `finalize.sh --scrub` only *reports* on text artifacts
  (`*.log`, `*.txt`) via gitleaks — a human must eyeball images/video before
  sharing them anywhere. Because `.evidence/` is gitignored, nothing reaches
  git history, but external sharing is on you.
- **`capture.sh web` needs Node + Playwright installed in the project.** If
  `playwright` doesn't resolve from the CWD it exits `4` with an install hint
  (`npm i -D playwright && npx playwright install chromium`) — or use the
  `microsoft/playwright-cli` skill as the browser engine instead.
- **`capture.sh screen` on macOS needs Screen Recording permission** and the
  right avfoundation device index (default `1`, varies per machine). List
  devices with `ffmpeg -f avfoundation -list_devices true -i ""` and pass
  `--device`. On Linux it uses `x11grab` on `$DISPLAY`.
- **Agent detection is best-effort.** Env markers (`$CLAUDECODE`, `$CURSOR_*`,
  `$CODEX_*`) then artifact presence; falls back to `unknown`. Pass
  `--agent cursor|codex|…` to `new-bundle.sh` when the session isn't yours.
- **`term` falls back to a plain log without asciinema.** The log still
  captures stdout+stderr and the command's exit code, but not timing/replay.
  Install `asciinema` for a replayable `.cast`.
- **Bundles default to `.evidence/.current`.** Running a second `new-bundle.sh`
  repoints `.current`; pass `--bundle DIR` to capture into an older bundle.
```
</details></tool-use>

# demo evidence

Reviewing an agent's work usually means reading the diff or booting the app
by hand. This skill has the agent **leave behind acceptance evidence** —
screenshots, screen/terminal recordings, request logs — filed into a
`.gitignore`-protected `.evidence/` tree, each bundle keyed to the git
branch/commit and the coding-agent session that produced it. A reviewer (or a
later agent) opens the bundle's `MANIFEST.md`, watches the demo, and signs off
— no re-driving the app.

The lifecycle is three scripts: **`new-bundle.sh`** (open a bundle) →
**`capture.sh`** (add artifacts, once per surface) → **`finalize.sh`** (stamp a
verdict and render the review page). Complements the global `run` / `verify`
skills: use *those* to drive the app; use *this* to record what they showed.

## When to use

- User says "record a demo of this", "leave evidence", "capture a
  screenshot/video of the feature", "prove it works", "demos over diffs".
- User wants **async 驗收 / sign-off** — they'll review later, not watch you now.
- You just finished a feature and want the acceptance artifacts to live
  next to the branch/commit that produced them.
- A reviewer asked "show me it works" without reading the diff.

## When NOT to use

- The change has **no runtime surface** (docs, comments, pure refactor with
  tests) → nothing to demo; point at the tests.
- You just need to *drive* the app to check it yourself → global `run` /
  `verify`. Only reach here when you want a **filed, reviewable artifact**.
- Posting media **into a PR** → not in v1. `.evidence/` is gitignored, so its
  images/videos have no public URL to embed (see Gotchas). Tracked as a `P?`
  backlog item.

77	before/after screenshot pair or a 10-second flow beats a folder of noise.
78	
79	### 3. Finalize for review
80	
81	```bash
82	bash skills/local/demo-evidence/scripts/finalize.sh \
83	  --verdict PASS \
84	  --step "open /login" --step "submit valid creds" --step "expect /dashboard" \
85	  --scrub
86	```
87	
88	Stamps the verdict, appends reproduction steps, refreshes artifact sizes, runs
89	an optional secret scan, and renders the human-facing `MANIFEST.md` (verdict
90	badge, context, repro steps, artifact table, review checklist). Point the
91	reviewer at `<bundle>/MANIFEST.md`.
92	
93	## Available scripts
94	
95	- **`scripts/new-bundle.sh`** — Create a bundle keyed to session + git; emit its path as JSON. Guarantees `.evidence/` is gitignored.
96	  - Flags: `--title`, `--feature`, `--agent`, `--root`, `--dry-run`, `--help`.
97	  - Exit: `0` ok, `1` bad args, `2` not a git repo, `3` jq missing.
98	- **`scripts/capture.sh <web|term|http|screen>`** — Capture one artifact into a bundle (default `.current`) and record it in `manifest.json`.
99	  - Common: `--bundle`, `--root`, `--name`, `--note`, `--dry-run`.
100	  - `web`: `--url`, `--steps`, `--timeout`. `term`: `--cmd`, `--log`. `http`: `--url`, `--method`, `--data`, `--header` (repeatable). `screen`: `--seconds`, `--device`, `--display`.
101	  - Exit: `0` ok, `1` bad args, `2` no bundle, `3` jq missing, `4` capture tool missing, `5` capture failed.
102	- **`scripts/finalize.sh`** — Set verdict, append steps, refresh sizes, optional secret scan, render `MANIFEST.md`.
103	  - Flags: `--bundle`, `--root`, `--verdict PASS|NEEDS_WORK|pending`, `--step` (repeatable), `--scrub`, `--dry-run`, `--help`.
104	  - Exit: `0` ok, `1` bad args, `2` no bundle, `3` jq missing.
105	- **`scripts/detect-session.sh`** — Best-effort `{agent, session_id, source, specstory_path}` JSON. Standalone or called by `new-bundle.sh`.
106	  - Flags: `--agent`, `--json`/`--tsv`, `--quiet`, `--help`. Exit: `0` always, `1` bad args.
107	
108	## Bundled assets
109	
110	- `assets/capture-web.mjs` — Minimal Playwright runner (screenshot + video +
111	  trace) invoked by `capture.sh web`. Loads `playwright` from the project's
112	  `node_modules` via `createRequire(cwd)`.
113	
114	## Gotchas
115	
116	- **`.evidence/` media has NO public URL — it cannot embed in a GitHub PR.**
117	  The whole point is a gitignored local surface, so images/videos aren't
118	  web-reachable. Posting to a PR (gist-raw-URL image embed, video links) is a
119	  deliberate `P?` backlog item, out of scope for v1. For now, share the bundle
120	  locally or push it out-of-band.
121	- **Screenshots and logs can leak secrets, and screenshots can't be
122	  auto-scrubbed.** `finalize.sh --scrub` only *reports* on text artifacts
123	  (`*.log`, `*.txt`) via gitleaks — a human must eyeball images/video before
124	  sharing them anywhere. Because `.evidence/` is gitignored, nothing reaches
125	  git history, but external sharing is on you.
126	- **`capture.sh web` needs Node + Playwright installed in the project.** If
127	  `playwright` doesn't resolve from the CWD it exits `4` with an install hint
128	  (`npm i -D playwright && npx playwright install chromium`) — or use the
129	  `microsoft/playwright-cli` skill as the browser engine instead.
130	- **`capture.sh screen` on macOS needs Screen Recording permission** and the
131	  right avfoundation device index (default `1`, varies per machine). List
132	  devices with `ffmpeg -f avfoundation -list_devices true -i ""` and pass
133	  `--device`. On Linux it uses `x11grab` on `$DISPLAY`.
134	- **Agent detection is best-effort.** Env markers (`$CLAUDECODE`, `$CURSOR_*`,
135	  `$CODEX_*`) then artifact presence; falls back to `unknown`. Pass
136	  `--agent cursor|codex|…` to `new-bundle.sh` when the session isn't yours.
137	- **`term` falls back to a plain log without asciinema.** The log still
138	  captures stdout+stderr and the command's exit code, but not timing/replay.
139	  Install `asciinema` for a replayable `.cast`.
140	- **Bundles default to `.evidence/.current`.** Running a second `new-bundle.sh`
141	  repoints `.current`; pass `--bundle DIR` to capture into an older bundle.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The regex issue is confirmed—the original pattern leaves the full basename intact, so the session ID captures the entire slug with title, which is the defect. The corrected regex with the optional suffix pattern produces the expected truncated result. Bash 3.2 actually preserves the quoted string as a single argument even within the parameter expansion, so the spacing behavior is working as intended.

For test3, the slug mismatch between the generated and expected values confirms a second defect. The SESSION_DIR ends up with an overly long name because the session component isn't being slugified—it retains the raw timestamp with underscores and the full title. The main issue traces back to the regex not properly truncating the basename before the session ID is constructed.

On git edge cases: unborn HEAD repos will fail the short SHA command but the BRANCH fallback handles it gracefully. Detached HEAD just returns "HEAD" as a label, which is fine. The `.gitignore` handling works correctly even when the file doesn't exist—grep exits with code 2, the negation makes the condition true, and the file gets created. There are a few robustness concerns worth noting: passing an absolute root path would produce malformed gitignore lines, there's a potential race condition on the `.current` file, and the `newest_file` function could have issues with zero matching files or filenames containing newlines, though these are lower priority edge cases.

Actually, I'm realizing there's a more serious portability bug here. The `find ... -print0 | xargs -0 ls -t | head -n1` pattern behaves differently between GNU and BSD xargs. On macOS with BSD xargs, if the directory exists but has no matching files, xargs won't run the command at all. But on Linux with GNU xargs, it runs `ls -t` with no arguments, which lists the current working directory instead—so it picks the newest file from CWD as a spurious result. This means on Linux, an empty directory could incorrectly return a random file from the current working directory, contaminating the session ID and agent detection. The script claims Bash 3.2 compatibility for macOS but could run on Linux, so this is a real portability defect that needs fixing.
</details></think>

Claim: http status is smuggled into free-text note instead of a structured manifest field; empty --note yields a leading space
Detail: add_artifact records note as "$NOTE status=$status". The artifact schema has no dedicated status field, so the only place status reaches the manifest is by string-appending 'status=NNN' to prose. (1) If --note is omitted, NOTE="" and the note becomes " status=307" with a leading space. (2) If a user's --note text itself contains 'status=' the value is ambiguous to parse. (3) Every other mode (web/term/screen) stores note verbatim, so 'status=' pollution is http-specific and inconsistent. The clean fix is to add a machine field (kind-specific) or record the .json sidecar (see first finding) rather than encode status in prose.
Failure scenario: Automation greps note for /status=(\d+)/ but the parent passed --note 'checks status=code path' — the regex now matches the wrong token. Or --note omitted, note = ' status=307', and a trim-sensitive consumer keeps the leading space.

I'm examining the gitleaks behavior in this script. The code pipes a file into gitleaks and treats any non-zero exit code as evidence of a secret, but the concern is that gitleaks might also return non-zero for operational errors—meaning legitimate failures could be misreported as security issues. I need to verify what exit codes gitleaks actually produces.

Looking at the gitleaks subcommand structure, the `stdin` command exists in recent versions but the naming may have changed across versions. If a script runs on a version where the subcommand name is different, every file would trigger a false alarm. The real problem is that when gitleaks fails for any reason, the hits counter increments, which suppresses the success message that would normally appear when no secrets are found. So a tooling failure gets silently converted into a security warning. gitleaks exit codes conflate leaks (exit 1) with operational errors (also exit 1), so the script can't distinguish between them. This means any gitleaks failure—whether from a missing subcommand, unsupported flag, or actual scan error—gets reported as "possible secret", which is misleading noise. The consequence is false alarms and suppressed success messages, though it does fail safely toward warning rather than silently hiding real secrets.

Let me verify the claim by checking if gitleaks is available and testing its actual exit behavior.

I'm seeing a key difference in how xargs behaves across systems: macOS's BSD version safely skips execution when given empty input, but GNU xargs on Linux runs the command once anyway, which causes `ls -t` to list the current directory and produce spurious results. This is a real portability issue since the skill gets distributed through npx and could run anywhere. The second test output confirms this behavior.

I'm also spot-checking a few other potential issues: the `--argjson dirty` parameter looks fine since DIRTY is set as unquoted true/false, the awk parsing of session_id from a TSV should be okay unless the value contains a tab (unlikely), and empty specstory_path values are handled correctly. The JSON output construction using printf and string interpolation could theoretically break if BRANCH or TITLE contains special characters like quotes or backslashes, though git ref naming rules actually allow double quotes in branch names—it's rare but possible. The session_id from specstory appears to be sanitized already.

Now I'm ranking the actual bugs I've found. The top issue is that the SpecStory timestamp regex expects full seconds (HH-MM-SS) but real filenames use minute precision (HH-MMZ), so the title-stripping regex fails and the full title slug leaks into the session_id and directory name. I've confirmed this against an actual manifest where the session.id shows the full slug. The second major bug is that cwd_slug only replaces forward slashes with hyphens, but Claude's actual project slug replaces every non-alphanumeric character including dots and underscores—so any repo path with those characters causes a slug mismatch, the Claude jsonl file isn't found, and the system loses the stable UUID and falls back to specstory/unknown.

Beyond those, there's a portability issue where GNU xargs on Linux will still run `ls` even with empty input, listing the current directory and producing a spurious newest file and wrong agent assignment, whereas BSD xargs on macOS handles this safely. The `.current` pointer file is written with a truncating redirect instead of atomically, so concurrent reads could see partial or empty content. The stdout JSON is hand-built with printf and could produce invalid JSON if branch names contain quotes or backslashes, though the manifest.json itself is safely generated with jq. There's also a minor issue with absolute paths in --root creating mismatched gitignore lines, and a potential edge case where `ls -t` piped through xargs might not find the true newest file if there are enough files to exceed ARG_MAX and force batching.

The cwd_slug transformation is confirmed to replace every non-alphanumeric character with a dash, not just slashes—the current sed pattern only handles slashes and misses dots, underscores, and spaces. I'll document these findings with absolute file paths and line numbers.

20	function parseArgs(argv) {
21	  const o = { timeout: 15000 };

23	    const a = argv[i];
24	    if (a === '--url') o.url = argv[++i];
25	    else if (a === '--out') o.out = argv[++i];

29	    else if (a === '--help' || a === '-h') o.help = true;
30	  }

32	}

38	  process.exit(opt.help ? 0 : 1);

44	const traceName = `${opt.name}-trace.zip`;
45	const videoName = `${opt.name}.webm`;
46

48	const context = await browser.newContext({ recordVideo: { dir: opt.out } });
49	await context.tracing.start({ screenshots: true, snapshots: true });
50	const page = await context.newPage();
51	
52	let ok = true;
53	try {
54	  await page.goto(opt.url, { waitUntil: 'load', timeout: opt.timeout });
55	  if (opt.steps) {

60	} catch (e) {

63	} finally {

65	  const video = page.video();
66	  await context.close();   // flushes the video file to disk
67	  await browser.close();

77	if (fs.existsSync(path.join(opt.out, traceName))) result.trace = traceName;

I'm noticing that markdown links with spaces in filenames break because the parser interprets the space as the end of the URL. According to CommonMark spec, the URL in an inline link needs either balanced parentheses or angle brackets to handle spaces properly — so `[out (final).png](out (final).png)` fails because the parser stops at the first space in the destination.
